result.result:
Changes made to `source-read` by event handlers now reach the final output for files pulled in with `.. include::`. The new tests pass, and the full test suite fails the same 12 tests with and without my change.

**Why it happened:** Sphinx emits `source-read` when it reads a document. But docutils' `include` directive reads the included file itself and feeds its lines straight into the parser. So when your handler ran for `something-to-include.rst`, it was editing that file as a separate document, and the copy inserted into `index.rst` was never touched.

**The fix** (`sphinx/directives/other.py`): `Include.run()` now wraps the parser's `insert_input()` call, which docutils uses to inject included lines. The text first goes through `source-read`, and the edited version is what gets parsed.
- **Only when needed:** the wrapper is installed only if something listens to `source-read`, and it's removed again right after the include runs.
- **Nested includes work:** each include runs its own pass, so an include inside an included file is also processed.
- **Marker lines kept:** docutils adds a blank line and an end-of-inclusion comment to the included text. These are left out of what handlers see and put back afterwards.
- **`docname` argument:** for an included file that is itself a document, handlers get that file's name (e.g. `baz/baz`). For a non-document such as `text.txt`, they get the including document's name, so they always receive a string, never `None`.
- **Literal includes are skipped:** `:literal:` and `:code:` includes don't use this path, so they don't trigger the event.

**Two side effects:**
- If an included `.rst` file is also built as its own page, `source-read` fires for it twice: once when it's read as a document and once each time it's included. A handler that isn't safe to run twice on the same text will need to cope with that.
- The fix works by swapping out a method on docutils' parser object while the include runs, because docutils has no proper way to hook into this. A future docutils release could break it.

**Tests:** I added a test project, `tests/roots/test-directive-include/`, with nested includes, a `.txt` include and the `&REPLACE_ME;` case from the issue, plus three tests in `tests/test_directive_other.py`:
- the event fires for included files and respects `:start-line:`;
- replacements apply through nested includes;
- a full HTML build leaves no `&REPLACE_ME;`.

All three fail without the fix and pass with it.

The 12 suite failures are in `test_highlighting` and `test_intl`, and they fail the same way on the original code, so they look like environment issues. I couldn't run ruff or mypy because they aren't installed in `.venv`.

I also added an entry to `CHANGES`. I used `#10678` as the issue number, which is my guess, so please correct it if it's wrong. Nothing is committed.
